title: The HL essay
summary: The HL-only formal essay: choosing a text and a line of inquiry, building an argument in 1,200–1,500 words, and meeting the four criteria.

keyterms.definition: A formal coursework essay of 1,200–1,500 words on one literary or non-literary text or work studied, worth 20% at HL.
The focused question that drives the HL essay, often developed from the learner portfolio.
A student's collection of responses and reflections across the course, used to develop ideas for assessments.
Acknowledging all sources accurately and submitting only your own work.
Criticism or commentary about a text; optional in the HL essay and must be cited.
A reference identifying the source of a quotation or idea.
How an argument grows logically from paragraph to paragraph rather than repeating points.
HL essay criterion C (5 marks): a coherent, well-developed argument that stays on the line of inquiry.

questions.prompt: What is the word count for the HL essay?
questions.explanation: Examiners stop reading beyond the upper limit, so stay within it.

questions.statement: The HL essay may be written on a literary work or a non-literary text or body of work studied in the course.
questions.explanation: You choose one text or work, but it cannot be one used in the individual oral or for Paper 2.

questions.text: The focused question that drives the HL essay is called the line of ___.
questions.explanation: A precise line of inquiry keeps the essay focused and analytical.

questions.prompt: Which is the strongest line of inquiry?
options: How does the novel's shifting narrative voice expose the limits of the narrator's self-knowledge?
questions.explanation: It is specific, focused on authorial choice and arguable within the word limit.

questions.prompt: Match the HL essay criterion to its focus (5 marks each).
questions.explanation: Four criteria of 5 marks give the essay's 20 marks.

questions.prompt: How can the learner portfolio help with the HL essay?
options: It stores reflections and explorations from which a line of inquiry can grow
It is submitted instead of the essay
questions.explanation: The portfolio is a record of thinking that feeds all assessments; it is not itself marked.

questions.statement: Using secondary sources is compulsory in the HL essay.
questions.explanation: Secondary sources are optional; if used, they must support your argument and be properly cited.

questions.text: Acknowledging all sources and submitting your own work is part of academic ___.
questions.explanation: Any quotation or borrowed idea must be referenced.

questions.prompt: Why should you avoid a line of inquiry that is mainly about the author's biography?
options: The essay rewards analysis of the text and its choices, not biography
It makes the essay too short
questions.explanation: Context can support analysis, but the focus must be the text.

items: Review the learner portfolio for ideas
Choose a text and draft a line of inquiry
Gather evidence and plan the argument
Write a draft and receive teacher feedback
Revise and submit the final essay
questions.explanation: Teachers may give one round of written feedback on a draft.

questions.prompt: What does "development" mean in criterion C?
options: Each paragraph advances the argument, building towards a fuller answer
questions.explanation: Development means ideas grow and deepen rather than circling the same point.

questions.statement: Quotations in the HL essay should be cited so the examiner can locate them.
questions.explanation: Consistent citation of primary and any secondary sources is required.

questions.text: Criticism or commentary written about a text is a ___ source.
questions.explanation: The text itself is the primary source.

questions.prompt: Which paragraph opening best shows development?
options: If the narrator's early confidence masks his doubts, the fractured syntax of the final chapter shows that mask finally slipping.
Next I will talk about chapter 4.
questions.explanation: It builds explicitly on a previous point, moving the argument forward.

questions.prompt: Match the essay part to its job.

pairs.right: Presents the line of inquiry and thesis
Develops one step of the argument

questions.explanation: A formal essay structure supports focus and academic honesty.

questions.prompt: What register is appropriate for the HL essay?
questions.explanation: Criterion D rewards clear, precise, formal academic language.

questions.statement: A conclusion should introduce a brand-new argument not mentioned in the essay.
questions.explanation: Conclusions synthesise; they may suggest wider significance but should not open new arguments.

questions.prompt: What should you do if your draft is 1,800 words?
options: Cut summary, repetition and weaker points to fit the limit
questions.explanation: Material beyond the limit is not assessed, and cutting usually sharpens focus.

questions.text: HL essay criterion C is called focus, organization and ___.
questions.explanation: Unlike Paper 1, the HL essay criterion C explicitly rewards development.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the HL essay is accurate?
options: It is externally assessed coursework worth 20% at HL
It is an internal assessment marked only by teachers
It is taken under exam conditions
questions.explanation: It is written over time but marked by IB examiners.
